title: Bedrock GPT

whenToUse: Single prompt to single completion from a GPT model, when the call must run in YOUR AWS account and region: summarise, rewrite, classify, answer. No streaming, no tools, no schema enforcement; reach for a heavier node when a step genuinely needs token streaming, iterative tool use, strict JSON output, or to read an image or document alongside the prompt.

inputs.description: Data from previous nodes that can be referenced in templates

model.title: Model
model.description: Select the GPT model to use

maxTokens.description: Hard ceiling on the reply. The model stops when it hits this, mid-sentence and without an error, so raise it for long output rather than leaving it to trim.

package.name: aws-bedrock
package.packageFile:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/package.schema.json

# BEDROCK AS MANIFESTS, and the cheapest AWS package to convert: both API calls it makes
# (Converse and InvokeModel) are plain signed JSON POSTs. Everything it needed already
# existed by the time it was reached — the signer from DynamoDB, and `transport: binary`
# for the attachments Claude can read.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/aws-bedrock/`.

name: aws-bedrock
displayName: AWS Bedrock
description: Claude and GPT models plus Titan embeddings on AWS Bedrock
version: 2.1.0
category: ai
publisher: unoverse
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749137717/gravity/icons/vdyfnijyuyk8ajqtp3nu.webp

features:
  - Claude on Bedrock via the native Messages API, with images, documents and tools
  - GPT on Bedrock, one prompt to one completion
  - Titan text embeddings, inline or over a service edge
  - Apply Bedrock guardrails to any text — screen, block or mask by your org's policy

# Two labels deep at least: bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com.
allowedHosts:
  - "**.amazonaws.com"
  # The bedrock-mantle endpoint, AWS's host for the native Anthropic Messages API:
  # bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws.
  - "**.api.aws"
  # Any host, for the UNAUTHENTICATED attachment fetches only. BedrockClaude reads an image
  # or document from a url a person supplies, which cannot be declared in advance. Those
  # calls send no credential, and the executor refuses "*" the moment one does.
  - "*"

requires:
  # SigV4 for the embeddings nodes; the LLM nodes authenticate with a Bedrock API key,
  # x-api-key on the Mantle endpoint and bearer on bedrock-runtime.
  credential: [awsSigV4, apiKeyHeader, bearer]
  transport: [json, binary]
  # Bedrock embeds ONE text per request, so a batch is a fan-out.
  chunk: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.awsCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

# Transcribed from plugin-base's shared AWSCredential, NAME AND FIELDS UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `awsCredential` keep resolving. Every AWS package
# shares this one, exactly as they shared the TypeScript definition.
#
# sessionToken is NEW, and additive. The retired definition had no such field, so anyone on
# temporary credentials (an assumed role, anything via STS) could not use these nodes at
# all. The signer sends and signs it only when it is filled in.

name: awsCredential
displayName: AWS Credentials
description: AWS credentials for AWS services (DynamoDB, S3, Bedrock, and the rest)
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html

properties:
  - name: accessKeyId
    displayName: Access Key ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Access Key ID
    placeholder: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
  - name: secretAccessKey
    displayName: Secret Access Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Secret Access Key
    placeholder: ""
  - name: region
    displayName: AWS Region
    type: string
    secret: false # Public: it appears in every AWS endpoint hostname.
    required: false
    default: us-east-1
    description: The region your tables live in
    placeholder: us-east-1
  - name: sessionToken
    displayName: Session Token
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: Only for temporary credentials from STS or an assumed role. Leave empty for a long-lived key.
    placeholder: ""
credentials.bedrockCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

# A Bedrock API key, NOT an IAM access-key pair. Minted on the Bedrock console's API keys
# page, it authenticates as a plain header with no SigV4 signing: `x-api-key` against the
# bedrock-mantle Anthropic endpoint, `Authorization: Bearer` against bedrock-runtime.
#
# The embeddings nodes keep the signed awsCredential; this one belongs to the LLM nodes.

name: bedrockCredential
displayName: AWS Bedrock
description: API key credentials for AWS Bedrock model calls
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: A Bedrock API key from the Bedrock console
    placeholder: ABSK...

  - name: region
    displayName: Region
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: The AWS region your Bedrock models are enabled in
    placeholder: us-east-1

shared.bedrock.yaml:
# The one call shape every Bedrock node makes.
#
# Bedrock is REST, unlike DynamoDB: the model id is in the PATH and the operation is the
# last segment, so there is no X-Amz-Target header here. `bedrock-runtime` is the signing
# service name and is NOT the same as the console's "bedrock" — signing against the wrong
# one is a 403 that says nothing about which name was wrong.

call: &call
  method: POST
  credential:
    scheme: awsSigV4
    service: bedrock-runtime
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  # Bedrock throttles hard under load and answers 429; retrying is the difference between a
  # workflow that survives a burst and one that fails a step at random.
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

host: &host >-
  return 'https://bedrock-runtime.' + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1') + '.amazonaws.com'

# The same call, authenticated with a Bedrock API key instead of request signing.
# bedrock-runtime accepts the key as a plain bearer header, so the executor needs no
# signer for the nodes that use this shape.
keyCall: &keyCall
  method: POST
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.bedrockCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
shared.models.yaml:
# The canonical Bedrock model lists, one per model family, organised by TIER.
#
# Same contract as openai/shared/models.yaml: the data lives here, the fallback logic
# (`resolve: modelTier` on the config field) lives in the executor. A new generation is
# a per-tier edit here, and every node plus every saved workflow moves over automatically.
#
# Bedrock ids carry the vendor prefix. Enable each model for your region in the Bedrock
# console before first use; that is an account setting, not something a manifest can do.

claude:
  # Listed large first so the strongest reads first. The picker's options.
  enum:
    - anthropic.claude-opus-5
    - anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
    - anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5

  # Version numbers in the labels by request. When a generation ships, the label is
  # edited alongside the id, or the two lie together.
  enumNames:
    - Claude Opus 5 (Frontier, complex work)
    - Claude Sonnet 5 (Balanced intelligence/cost)
    - Claude Haiku 4.5 (Cost-optimized, high-volume)

  # Balanced middle tier, the sensible default for most work.
  default: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

gpt:
  enum:
    - openai.gpt-5.6-sol
    - openai.gpt-5.6-terra
    - openai.gpt-5.6-luna

  enumNames:
    - GPT-5.6 Sol (Frontier, complex work)
    - GPT-5.6 Terra (Balanced intelligence/cost)
    - GPT-5.6 Luna (Cost-optimized, high-volume)

  default: openai.gpt-5.6-terra

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in the order interface.yaml declares them.
#
# Converse replies put the answer in output.message.content, a LIST of blocks; a long
# answer can arrive in several text blocks, so they concatenate.

- emit: text
  value: >-
    return ((((response.output || {}).message || {}).content) || [])
      .filter(b => b.text).map(b => b.text).join('')

- emit: usage
  value: >-
    return {
      inputTokens: (response.usage || {}).inputTokens || 0,
      outputTokens: (response.usage || {}).outputTokens || 0,
      totalTokens: (response.usage || {}).totalTokens
        || (((response.usage || {}).inputTokens || 0) + (((response.usage || {}).outputTokens) || 0))
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# One call: Converse at bedrock-runtime, authenticated with the Bedrock API key as a
# bearer header. GPT models on Bedrock do not get the Anthropic Messages endpoint, which
# serves Claude only; Converse is AWS's one shape across the rest of the catalogue.
#
# No temperature: the GPT 5.6 family accepts only the default, so there is nothing to
# configure. Mirrors the OpenAI node.

- $ref: bedrock#keyCall
  name: generate
  url: >-
    return 'https://bedrock-runtime.' + (credentials.bedrockCredential.region || 'us-east-1')
      + '.amazonaws.com/model/' + encodeURIComponent(config.model) + '/converse'

  body: >-
    return Object.assign({
      messages: [{
        role: 'user',
        content: [{ text: config.prompt }]
      }],
      inferenceConfig: { maxTokens: config.maxTokens }
    },
    config.systemPrompt ? { system: [{ text: config.systemPrompt }] } : {})

  timeoutMs: 120000
files.config.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  # `prompt` is required for the same reason it is on OpenAI: this node has nothing to do
  # without one, and requiring it moves the complaint from a vendor 400 to config
  # validation, where the canvas can show it.
  required: [model, prompt]

  properties:
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: Select the GPT model to use
      enum: { $ref: models#gpt/enum }
      enumNames: { $ref: models#gpt/enumNames }
      default: { $ref: models#gpt/default }
      # A retired id falls back to the current best model in its tier, so replacing a
      # model generation cannot break a saved workflow.
      resolve: modelTier

    maxTokens:
      type: number
      title: Max Tokens
      description: >-
        Hard ceiling on the reply. The model stops when it hits this, mid-sentence and
        without an error, so raise it for long output rather than leaving it to trim.
      default: 1200
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 128000

    systemPrompt:
      type: string
      title: System Prompt
      description: >-
        Standing instructions for every run: the model's role, tone and limits. Optional.
        Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.markdownGuidelines}}.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    prompt:
      type: string
      title: Prompt
      description: The request to answer. Usually wired in from an upstream node.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
ui:order: [model, maxTokens, systemPrompt, prompt]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes that can be referenced in templates
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: text
    type: string
    description: The generated text response

  - name: usage
    type: object
    description: Token burn (inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens)

credentials:
  - name: bedrockCredential
    required: true
    displayName: AWS Bedrock
files.node.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/node.schema.json

type: BedrockOpenAI
kind: PromiseNode

name: Bedrock GPT
category: AI
color: "#01A88D"

description: One prompt in, one GPT completion out, running in your AWS account

whenToUse: >-
  Single prompt to single completion from a GPT model, when the call must run in YOUR AWS
  account and region: summarise, rewrite, classify, answer. No streaming, no tools, no
  schema enforcement; reach for a heavier node when a step genuinely needs token
  streaming, iterative tool use, strict JSON output, or to read an image or document
  alongside the prompt.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: a model call is non-deterministic, so a reused answer is a different
  # answer presented as the same one.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/test.schema.json

testData:
  config:
    model: openai.gpt-5.6-luna
    prompt: Reply with exactly the word READY and nothing else.
    systemPrompt: You follow instructions precisely.
    maxTokens: 64
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    text: "return output.text.trim().length > 0"
    usage: "return output.usage.totalTokens > 0"
